title: Understanding Drain Traps and Trap Seals
description: Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system requires a drain trap. The primary purpose of this curved section of pipe is to hold a specific volume of water, creating a crucial physical barrier known as a trap seal. This water seal prevents hazardous sewer gases, foul odors, and insects from entering the living space through the fixture opening. When fixtures go unused for extended periods, the trap water can evaporate, breaking the seal and allowing odors to escape. Regular use or refilling dried traps is a simple maintenance habit that preserves indoor air quality.

Understanding Drain Traps and Trap Seals

Every plumbing fixture connected to a drainage system requires a drain trap. The primary purpose of this curved section of pipe is to hold a specific volume of water, creating a crucial physical barrier known as a trap seal. This water seal prevents hazardous sewer gases, foul odors, and insects from entering the living space through the fixture opening. When fixtures go unused for extended periods, the trap water can evaporate, breaking the seal and allowing odors to escape. Regular use or refilling dried traps is a simple maintenance habit that preserves indoor air quality.
